This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 1,00,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic Dinesha S.M vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135898430/

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 24.11.2022 at about 11.30 a.m., when the Petitioner was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 09-JJ-7555 and when he reached near Sulekere road,
K.R. Pete, Nagamangala main road, at that time, one KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-11-F-0430 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner and at high speed and dashed against the SCCH 15 3 MVC No.744/2023 Petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to the said impact, the Petitioner fell down and had sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Government Hospital, Nagamangala and after first aid he was shifted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital and Research Centre, wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
He had spent Rs.7,00,000/- towards medical treatment and other incidental expenses.
4. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as an Agriculturist / Milk Vendor and was earning of Rs.35,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries he becomes permanent disabled.
The said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-11-F-0430 by its driver.
The Respondent is the owner cum internal insurer of the offending vehicle and therefore, Respondent is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.

In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondent, it appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed Objection statement inter-alia denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the said accident and also the expenses incurred for the treatment of the Petitioner.

Further it contended that, on the alleged date the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-11-F-0430 was in its schedule trip from Nagamangala towards K.R.Pete at about 11.00 a.m. and when it reached near Sulekere the Petitioner fell down from motorcycle on the middle of the road.
Then, the KSRTC bus driver has stopped the bus and other passengers get down and called the Ambulance and shifted the Petitioner to the Government hospital.
The KSRTC bus driver is not at all responsible for the said accident.
Further, it contended that, after lapse of 10 days the Petitioner lodged false Complaint against the KSRTC bus driver.
Further, it contended that the Petitioner rode the bike without wearing helmet and SCCH 15 5 MVC No.744/2023 without Driving License.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay any compensation to the Petitioner.
On these grounds, Respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

6. On the rival Pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:

sentences.text:
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 24.11.2022 at about 11.30 a.m. near Sulekere road,
K.R. Pete, Nagamangala main road, Nagamangala Town and Taluk, Mandya, due to the rash and negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-11-F-0430 by its driver?
2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for? If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
3) What Order or Award?

In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 25 documents at Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-25 and also examined 2 witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and got marked 6 documents at Ex.P26 to 31 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent has examined two witnesses as RW.1 and 2 and got marked 15 documents at Ex.R1 to 15 and closed its side evidence.

8. Having heard the arguments by the learned Counsels for both sides and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Negative.
Issue No.2 : In the Negative.
Issue No.3 :
10. On the other hand, the Respondent has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending KSRTC Bus.
11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 25 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.25.
P.W.1 has re-iterated the Petition averments in his chief-affidavit.

Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-25 are the Certified copies of FIR, Complaint, Vehicle Seizer Mahazar, Wound certificate, Police Notices and Replies, IMV report, Statements, Requisition, Spot mahazar with Sketch, Charge-sheet, Prescriptions, Medical bills, Discharge summaries, Aadhaar card and X-rays.

12. Upon going through Ex.P-1 & 2 i.e., FIR and Complaint which shows that on the Complaint Dinesha S.M vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135898430/
3 lodged by the brother of the Petitioner by name Ganesha S/o Late Muthuraju before Nagamangala Town Police Station, the PSI of the concerned SCCH 15 8 MVC No.744/2023 Police Station has registered the case against the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-11-F-0430 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 of IPC and under Sec.187 of IMV Act.

Ex.P.5 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Ex.P10 is the IMV report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to the any mechanical defects of the vehicles.
Ex.P11 to 14 are the Statements of the Petitioner and eye witnesses stating about the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the offending KSRTC bus.
Ex.P15 is the Requisition given to the RTO.

Ex.P-17 is the true copy of the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Nagamangala Town Police Station has submitted Charge- SCCH 15 9 MVC No.744/2023 sheet against the driver of the offending Bus for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 338 of IPC and under Sec.187 of IMV Act.

13. Further, the Petitioner has examined MRO by name Govindaraju as PW.2 and doctor by name Dr. S.A. Somashekara as P.W.3 and got marked 8 documents at Ex.P.26 to 31.
14.
P.W.1 is subjected for cross-examination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent.

It is the main contention of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending KSRTC Bus.

On the other hand, it is the specific contention of the Respondent that on the alleged date of accident, the KSRTC bus driver drove his bus slowly and carefully from Nagamangala towards KR pete main road at about 11.00 a.m. and when it came near Sulekere, the SCCH 15 10 MVC No.744/2023 KSRTC bus moving on the same direction and before that the Petitioner fell from the motor cycle on the middle of the road and then the KSRTC bus driver has stopped the bus and other passengers get down and as per the suggestion of the conductor and other passengers, the driver called the Ambulance and shifted the Petitioner to the Government hospital, Nelamangala in an Ambulance and therefore the KSRTC bus driver was not at all responsible for the said accident.

In order to substantiate the contention of the Respondent it has examined the driver of the KSRTC bus by name Harisha as RW.1 and he has reiterated the Objection Statement contentions in his chief-affidavit.

Further he got marked the Copy of Complaint sent to the CPI, DYSP and SP at Ex.R1 to 3, 2 Postal receipts at Ex.R4 and 5, 3 Postal Acknowledgments at Ex.R6 to 8, Acknowledgment at Ex.R9, Wound Certificate at Ex.R10, 4 photos at Ex.R11, CD at Ex.R12, Hospital Register of Nagamangala at Ex.R13, Certified copies of Feed back of referred cases and MLC Register extract SCCH 15 11 MVC No.744/2023 at Ex.R14 and 15.

Further the Respondent has examined CMO of Nagamangala by name S.Prasad as RW.2 and in the chief- examination RW.2 has deposed that on 24.11.2022 at about 1.20 p.m., the Petitioner came to his hospital for the treatment of the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident.

Further he deposed that Ex.R13 was issued by the Government hospital, Nagamangala and he has issued Ex.R14-MLC Register Extract and as per the Dinesha S.M vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135898430/
4 said document he got admitted the Petitioner in their hospital.
Further he deposed that the Petitioner was referred from Nagamangala hospital to their hospital.
He further deposed that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in their hospital from 24.11.2022 to 05.01.2023.
Further he deposed that he has not given treatment to the Petitioner.
He also deposed that in MLC Register, he has written History of Accident as Hit by Lorry and thereafter he striked out the word Lorry and he has written KSRTC bus over it.
Further he deposed that since the police have confirmed about SCCH 15 12 MVC No.744/2023 the vehicle which caused the accident he has mentioned KSRTC bus in the said document.
He further deposed that they would mention in the MLC Register as per the statement of the injured.
If the Statement given by the injured was not correct then they would mention as per the information given by the police.
It is pertinent to note here that, in the cross-examination by the Learned Counsel for the Petitioner, RW.2 has deposed that when the Petitioner came to their hospital he was conscious.
If the Petitioner was conscious then he would have mention how the accident was occurred and by which vehicle the accident was occurred, if truly the KSRTC bus was involved.
But, initially in the MLC Register Extract the History of Accident was mentioned as Hit by Lorry and later it was corrected by over writting.
Hence, it raises doubt about the veracity of the involvment of the alleged bus in the said accident.
15. Added to it, in the cross-examination, PW.1 has deposed that the Complaint was lodged by the public.
Further SCCH 15 13 MVC No.744/2023 he deposed that the Complaint was lodged by himself.
In further he has deposed that Ganesh was his brother and his brother lodged Complaint.
He further deposed that himself and his brother and the public lodged the Complaint.
So, the evidence of PW.1 itself is self contradictory.
Upon going through the Ex.P1 and 2, the Complaint was lodged by the brother of the Petitioner by name Ganesh on 29.11.2022.
The alleged accident was occurred on 24.11.2022 i.e., there was 5 days delay in lodging the Complaint.
However, the Complainant has stated that since he was engaged in the hospital for providing treatment to his brother, there was a delay in lodging the Complaint.
Ex.P5 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner pertaining to the Government hospital, Nagamangala, wherein the Petitioner was first taken for treatment from the alleged spot.
The said document shows that RTA / Self fall from the Honda bike.
Further it shows that he was brought in 108 Ambulance.

Ex.R1 to 3 are the Copy of Complaints given by the driver of the SCCH 15 14 MVC No.744/2023 KSRTC bus to the CPI, DYSP and SP stating that when he was driven the KSRTC bus from towards K.R.Pet and reached near Sulekere,
before that one rider fell on the middle of the road along with un-numbered motor cycle and while seeing the said injured, he stopped his bus and as per the suggestion of the conductor and passengers he called Ambulance and sent injured to the hospital in an Ambulance.
Ex.R10 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner which already marked as Ex.P5 in the evidence of PW.1 wherein it shows that Road Traffic Accident as "Self fall from the Honda bike."

Further Ex.R13 is the Hospital Register wherein it was mentioned as:
"History of ? self fall from Hero Honda Splendor bike near Sulekere, Nagamangala, at around 11.30 am on 24.11.2022."

16. Ex.R15 is the MLC Register wherein it was clearly shows that H/O "RTA Fall from bike due to hit by a lorry at about 11.30 a.m. on 24.11.2022 at Nagamangala, Kunigal SCCH 15 15 MVC No.744/2023 Road".
Thereafter, the Lorry was striked out and KSRTC bus was written over it and Dinesha S.M vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135898430/
5 Nagamangala was striked out and written Sulekere-Bogadi road over it.
But, this correction was not counter signed by the RW.2 who has striked out and written over it.

RW.2 has also admitted the said fact in his evidence and also he stated that as per the information given by the police he has striked out and he has over written KSRTC bus, MLC Register is a primary document and it cannot be altered.
Moreover, the alteration made by the RW.2 has not been counter signed.
So, involvement of the KSRTC bus itself is doubtful.

Upon going through the Ex.P27 i.e., Inpatient record of the Petitioner relating to the Adichunchanagiri Hospital, it contains the Requisition given by the Petitioner to the Superintendent of the said hospital requesting for correction in the MLC Register in respect of wrong information mentioned.
But, RW.2 has deposed that as per the confirmation made by the police, he has corrected the same in the MLC Register.
But, SCCH 15 16 MVC No.744/2023 Ex.P27 shows that the Requisition was given by the Petitioner for the said correction.
So, the evidence of RW.2 and the Ex.P27 is contradictory to each other.
Though the Petitioner got marked the Statement of the eye witnesses as Ex.P12 to 14, he has not examined any one of eye witnesses to the alleged accident.
Moreover, the Petitioner has not examined I.O.
Moreover, the PW.1 in his cross-examination admitted the suggestion that by colluding with the Police he has given false Complaint against the offending bus driver.
So, oral and documentary evidence led by both parties, there is no cogent evidence to show the involvement of the KSRTC bus in the alleged accident.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has failed to prove that he has sustained injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-11-F-0430.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Negative'.
SCCH 15 17 MVC No.744/2023 17. Issue No.2
: In view of detailed discussion as stated supra and my answer to Issue No.1 is in the "Negative", the Petitioner is not entitled for compensation.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "in the Negative".
18. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed with costs.
Draw award accordingly.
